heading: Setting · Seringapatam under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, as seen in 1800

items.label: City
items.title: The city: Seringapatam, the island fort on the Cauvery
items.alt: Hypothetical reconstruction of Seringapatam: a fort of long straight walls and bastions on a rocky Cauvery island, with a granite-pillar bridge and a temple tower inside
items.attested: An island about 3 miles by 1 in the Cauvery, a large rapid river with a wide rocky bed; the fort at its upper end, long straight walls and square bastions, cavaliers heaped one above another, ditches cut through the granite, a high steep glacis, an inner rampart and wide inner ditch; a bridge of square granite pillars with long stones laid across them and an aqueduct beside the road; streets narrow and confused, houses mostly mean; the Śrī Raṅga temple of great antiquity (Francis Buchanan, A Journey from Madras through the Countries of Mysore, Canara and Malabar, 1807, vol. 1 pp. 58–66).
items.prescribed: Buchanan saw the town in May 1800, a year after Tipu's fall and the siege, and describes it as he found it.
items.conjecture: The regularity of the walls (Buchanan calls the work 'unsightly'), the houses, the gateway tower's form, boats, dress.
items.note: Hypothetical reconstruction, painted with an AI image model from the texts above; not an archaeological finding. Colours, ornament and dress are illustrative.

items.label: Palace and tomb
items.title: The Lal Bagh palace and Hyder's mausoleum
items.alt: Hypothetical reconstruction of the Lal Bagh palace and the mausoleum of Hyder Ali with black polished columns, canals and a formal garden
items.attested: At the lower end of the island, outside the walls, the Laul Bagh palace 'though built of mud, possesses a considerable degree of elegance' and is 'the handsomest native building' he had seen; the garden laid out with canals from the river; near it the mausoleum of Hyder, where Tipu also lies, ornamented with columns of black hornblende that takes a splendid polish; the tombs covered with rich cloths, mullahs praying and musicians playing the nobat; nearby the Dariya Daulat Bagh with painted walls (Buchanan, vol. 1 pp. 73–74).
items.prescribed: Buchanan saw these buildings in 1800 and describes them as he found them.
items.conjecture: The palace reads as carved white stone here though Buchanan says mud; the dome, cypresses, planting layout and dress are conjecture.
items.note: Hypothetical reconstruction, painted with an AI image model from the texts above; not an archaeological finding. Colours, ornament and dress are illustrative.
